headline: AI leadership jitters overshadow a beat as Anthropic debuts
body: Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter report beat on both lines — adjusted EPS of $2.68 versus roughly $2.47 expected, and revenue of $115.8 billion against estimates near $109 billion, with interim CEO Colette Kress lifting the fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75% from 70%. The market's response was a decline anyway: shares gave back an early premarket pop and closed lower for a second straight session, extending a slide of more than 13% over the past week in the first earnings call since Jensen Huang's departure. That gap between solid fundamentals and weak price action is the clearest signal in the tape right now — investors appear to be pricing leadership uncertainty and governance questions (including a reported SEC inquiry into prior disclosures) as heavily as the numbers themselves, against a backdrop where the VIX spiked from the mid-teens to near 28 earlier this month and hasn't fully settled.

Attention today is on Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, with shares pricing yesterday and opening for trading this morning — a live test of whether investors still want fresh, pure-play AI exposure or are rotating away from it after a rough few weeks for the sector. The setup cuts both ways: several of this year's largest AI-adjacent IPOs are trading below their offer prices, suggesting the easier enthusiasm seen earlier in 2026 has cooled, even as demand into Anthropic's own pricing was described as strong. Retail chatter on the day reads as thin and inconclusive rather than clearly euphoric or fearful, so this take leans more on price action and company-specific news than on social-sentiment signal. Net effect: a market treating execution and leadership stability as the swing factor right now, more than broad macro headlines.
